ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there is a cyclopentane skeleton; a carbon at the upper right of the ring is connected to an oxygen anion-related fragment above, and is connected to an OEt group to the right; at the lower right of the same ring there is also a CO2Et ester substituent. There are also curved arrows in the figure, but the problem requires ignoring the arrows; hydrogen-related bonds are also not counted. Reasoning count: Count the bonds between heavy atoms by fragments. The cyclopentane ring itself has 5 C-C bonds. The upper substituent/transition-state central fragment has 4 heavy-atom bonds: central C-O, central C-OEt, the O-C bond in O-Et, and the internal C-C bond of the ethyl group. The lower CO2Et fragment has 5 heavy-atom bonds: ring C-carbonyl C, C=O, C-O, O-ethyl C, and the internal C-C of the ethyl group. The total is 5 + 4 + 5 = 14.

method.method_draft: First describe the image fragments, then count bonds fragmentwise: 5 C-C bonds in the cyclopentane ring; 4 heavy-atom bonds in the upper substituent/transition-state center (central C-O, central C-OEt, O-Et C bond, ethyl C-C); and 5 heavy-atom bonds in the lower CO2Et substituent (ring-C to carbonyl C, C=O, C-O, O-ethyl C, ethyl C-C). Sum 5 + 4 + 5 = 14.
